entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 22_Kalliope_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 1286 vertices and 2568 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 150 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (195°, 4°), period 4.1482 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 76.36974211932504 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: 20 camera-1 deconvolved frames, 4 nights from 2018-03-15 to 2018-05-05, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. The other 15 released camera-1 frames are not used: a lens keeps one apparition and at most 32 frames. Earlier finding, kept: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/22Kalliope/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 22_Kalliope_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked. Reopened 2026-09-18 because its condition was met: the SPHERE photograph lens rides this ADAM mesh, the model the survey’s rotation record and Figure B.18 describe; the Shape and Elevation views keep MPCD.

entries.subject: Released SAGE companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 22_Kalliope_sage.obj, which the imported ledger omitted. Its existence establishes a numerical candidate; method, calibration and independence from the selected MPCD reconstruction still need comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: The SAGE companion’s paper, scale and shape constraints have been compared with the selected MPCD release.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 20 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 16 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 205 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.16 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.39; 0 of 16 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. The lens stands on the silhouette registration recorded in the entry above and on the route proven against the Dawn mosaic on Vesta; this test adds no independent check for this body. Removed on 2026-09-16: a lens ships only when every registration measurement that reaches a verdict places it within three degrees, and this one measured outline systematic 4.58° against relief 1.00°.

entries.subject: de Kleer et al. (2024) ALMA thermal-inertia and dielectric-constant maps
entries.finding: The paper maps both properties on a 5-degree grid from ALMA 1.3 mm images (program 2018.1.01271.S) on the Ferrais et al. (2022) SAGE shape, with a northern region of high dielectric constant, the same method as Psyche's shipped lenses. No numerical grid is released: the arXiv text, the PSJ article page and its Crossref references name no data deposit. Figures are not cast.
entries.revisitWhen: The map grids are deposited as data.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.18 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.18, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.940 to 0.953 at our phase, against 0.946 to 0.959 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 5 of 5 columns. With the paper’s photographs 0.933 to 0.946. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -2.5 to 2.5° and its model panels at 0.0 to 2.5°. The spin axis we project lies at 71.5 to 112.6° on the sky against 64.6 to 129.5° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 1.417 px mean over 20 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 1.218 px at 2°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 0.67° from the published pole.
